learning: Race 6 showed that seven sensors at 10 mm pitch lowered oval and s-bend without fixing slalom (line loss 1.25). Slalom has now been tested against sensor reach, spread, density, lead and controller gain. The next race tests whether more steering authority and lower speed fix slalom. If slalom line loss falls below 1, keep the gains and tune base_speed for completion time. If not, the next step is a controller response change, not geometry.
notes: Race 5 geometry held unchanged, with controller tuned for slalom: kp 3.2, kd 0.6, base_speed 0.95. Next-race rule: if slalom line loss is still 1 or more with max_error at the limit, the geometry is not the limiter, so hold it and tune further. If oval finishes fall below 18 of 20 or s-bend finish time exceeds about 2.8 s, return kd and base_speed toward race 5 values.
rationale: Race 5 (606.82) is the best measured design: five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03, y = 0.06, kp 2.8, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.0. Oval finished 20/20 and s-bend 15/20, but slalom finished 0/20 with 1.15 line-loss events and max_error at the 0.06 m limit. Race 6 (seven sensors, 389.47) lowered oval and s-bend and did not reduce slalom line loss (1.25), so sensor density is not the slalom limiter. The Builder has reverted to the race 5 geometry, so this iteration tests controller response alone. The agreed rule for line loss at 1 or more with max_error at the limit is to raise kp toward 3.2 or lower base_speed toward 0.9. I do both moderately: kp 2.8 to 3.2 for more steering authority at the slalom bends, kd 0.5 to 0.6 to damp the extra gain and hold oval oscillation (0.29 in race 5), and base_speed 1.0 to 0.95 for more recovery time. Oval finished in about 2.2 s at base 1.0, so 0.95 should stay under 3 s with margin. s-bend mean finish was 2.49 s, so it is the tightest time margin. Expected result, not yet measured: slalom line loss below 1 and some slalom finishes, with oval holding at 18 or more of 20. If s-bend finish time becomes limiting, return base_speed to 1.0.
